content.user_title: Review Code Across Five Quality Axes
content.value_statement: Code changes can hide correctness, security, architecture, readability, and performance issues. This skill applies a structured review process and produces prioritized, actionable feedback.
actual_capabilities: Reviews changes for correctness, readability, architecture, security, and performance.
Categorizes feedback as critical, required, optional, informational, or minor.
Checks tests, edge cases, error paths, builds, and manual verification evidence.
Recommends structural remedies for duplication, tangled conditionals, weak boundaries, and oversized files.
Evaluates dependency additions and upgrades, including changelogs, lockfiles, licenses, and vulnerabilities.
Produces a clear approval or request-changes recommendation.
limitations: It cannot prove runtime correctness without access to executable tests and the project environment.
It depends on supplied requirements, diffs, tests, and repository context.
Specialized security or performance audits may require dedicated tools and deeper analysis.
Final merge decisions remain the responsibility of a human reviewer.

use_cases.title: Review a feature pull request
use_cases.description: Assess behavior, tests, architecture, security, and performance before approving a feature.

use_cases.title: Audit generated code
use_cases.description: Check agent-produced changes for plausible mistakes, hidden assumptions, weak tests, and unnecessary complexity.

use_cases.title: Evaluate a dependency upgrade
use_cases.description: Review changelog impact, lockfile changes, transitive packages, security exposure, and verification quality.

prompt_templates.title: Basic five-axis review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this change for correctness, readability, architecture, security, and performance. List required issues first, then optional improvements.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a focused pull request with clear requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Requirements and test review
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare this implementation with the requirements and tests. Identify missed edge cases, weak error handling, and missing regression coverage.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for features or bug fixes where behavior matters most.

prompt_templates.title: Structural refactor review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this refactor for complexity reduction, module ownership, type boundaries, duplicated logic, and dead code. Propose specific structural remedies.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when code moves across modules or introduces abstractions.

prompt_templates.title: Dependency upgrade audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this dependency upgrade. Assess changelog risks, lockfile changes, transitive dependencies, security exposure, test coverage, and rollback clarity.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for package upgrades and supply-chain-sensitive changes.

output_examples.input: Review a bug fix that changes date parsing and adds one happy-path test.
output_examples.output: Required: add invalid, empty, and timezone-boundary tests. The implementation appears readable, but current coverage would not prevent the reported regression.

output_examples.input: Review a refactor that moves feature logic into a shared utility.
output_examples.output: Request changes: the refactor relocates complexity and weakens module ownership. Keep the logic in the feature package and reuse the existing canonical helper.

output_examples.input: Review a single-package dependency upgrade with a green test suite.
output_examples.output: Approve after confirming the changelog and lockfile diff. Tests pass, the upgrade is isolated, and rollback remains clear.

best_practices: Provide the change requirements, diff, tests, and relevant project conventions.
Review tests before implementation to understand intended behavior and coverage gaps.
Prioritize correctness and security findings before structural suggestions and minor style comments.
anti_patterns: Do not approve changes based only on passing tests.
Do not combine feature work, broad refactoring, and multiple dependency upgrades in one review.
Do not report vague concerns without evidence, severity, and a concrete remedy.

faq.question: What review dimensions does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers correctness, readability, architecture, security, performance, verification, change sizing, and dependency discipline.

faq.question: Does it run tests or builds automatically?
faq.answer: No. It evaluates provided verification evidence and can recommend commands or missing checks when project access permits.

faq.question: Can it review AI-generated code?
faq.answer: Yes. It applies the same standards while checking for plausible logic, hidden assumptions, and weak verification.

faq.question: How are findings prioritized?
faq.answer: Correctness and security come first, followed by structural regressions, missed simplifications, performance concerns, and optional style feedback.

faq.question: When should a change be approved?
faq.answer: Approve when the change improves code health, meets requirements, resolves required issues, and has credible verification.

faq.question: Can it replace a specialist security audit?
faq.answer: No. Security-sensitive changes may need dedicated threat modeling, dependency scanning, and runtime testing.
